basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5-6.' and it opens 'Vers. 5, 6. Et concidit vultus ejus in terram. Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 5, 6. Et concidit vultus ejus in terram. Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es, et concidit facies tua? Id est, Cur livore torqueris, et non bona verecundia perfunderis? Ut enim Sapientia dicit: Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam (Eccli. IV, 25).
